subject: addqtl: what is strong evidence for additional qtl

messages.author: bb6cce4079fc308e
messages.subject: addqtl: what is strong evidence for additional qtl
parts:
Dear Karl,

I have a follow-up question after my previous post about error when running stepwiseqtl. As I am working on 4-way cross, which stepwiseqtl doesn't aim at. So I guess the only way to employ MQM is to use makeqtl and addqtl.

The procedure I followed is that I make a preliminary multiple QTL model using makeqtl based on the result of scanone and scantwo and then refine the model using refineqtl. The next step is to estimate the effect of all QLTs and interactions by fitqtl including a drop-one test. Then I check for additional qtl by running addqtl. If I find some qtls with very high LOD score, then I go back to makeqtl and revise the formula by adding those QTL with high LOD. Those procedures are implemented iteratively unless no more additional qtls found by addqtl. Then the final model is refined by refineqtl and its effect is estimated. Do such procedures make sense?

However, I am not sure how to determine the threshold of LOD score when searching additional qtl with "addqtl". The other information I can use is to check the phenotypic traits accross genotypes at potential QTL with relatively high LOD found by "addqtl". Do you have any suggestions on determining LOD threshold or other threshold for clear evidence of additional qtls?

Thank you a lot!

Best wishes,
Xiaodong

I use a penalized LOD score, penalizing each QTL by the significance threshold obtained from a permutation test with a single-QTL scan. See the chapter 9 of the R/qtl book, http://rqtl.org/book

I hope to fix stepwiseqtl() and related functions to work properly for four-way cross data, but I've not had time to work on it yet.

karl
